metadata.title: Client Assessment Schema
metadata.purpose: Standardized client profile for Claude Code to read and generate personalized fitness programs. Populated from client onboarding intake.
metadata.instructions_for_claude: Read this schema in full before generating any program. Every field informs programming decisions. Cross-reference goal_mapping to select the correct program file. Flag any injury_limitations and cross-reference injury_navigation.json. Apply population_flags if present — these override standard programming rules.

primary_goal.notes: If client goal does not map cleanly, cross-reference client_program_goals.json for best fit secondary match.

secondary_goals.notes: Secondary goals layer on top of primary program. Do not replace primary structure — modify and supplement it.

definitions.Beginner: Less than 1 year of consistent training, or returning after a long break
definitions.Intermediate: 1-3 years of training, comfortable with most movements
definitions.Advanced: 3+ years, strong technique, familiar with periodization

programming_impact.Beginner: Prioritize movement quality, lower complexity, higher success rate exercises, 2-3 days/week minimum, longer warm-ups
programming_impact.Intermediate: Introduce periodization, supersets, and moderate complexity, 3-5 days/week
programming_impact.Advanced: Full periodization, advanced techniques (drop sets, tempo, RIR), 4-6 days/week

training_schedule.programming_notes: Never exceed available days. Build program around session length — a 30-min session looks very different from a 90-min session. Prioritize compound movements when session length is under 45 minutes.

equipment_definitions.Full Gym: All equipment available — barbells, cables, machines, dumbbells, racks
equipment_definitions.Home Gym: Dumbbells, some machines, limited cable access
equipment_definitions.Mixed: Varies week to week — build program with minimal equipment as baseline, note full gym upgrades

equipment_access.programming_impact: Filter all exercise selections through available equipment. Never program equipment the client does not have access to.

injuries_and_limitations.notes: If any injury or limitation is listed, set flag_for_injury_navigation to true and cross-reference injury_navigation.json before finalizing exercise selection.

programming_impact.Poor: Reduce volume and intensity. Prioritize recovery. Flag for stress and recovery secondary goal.
programming_impact.Inconsistent: Moderate volume. Build in deload awareness. Note in program.
programming_impact.Great: Can support higher volume and intensity.

programming_impact.High: Reduce session complexity. Shorter sessions. More low-impact options. Flag stress and recovery secondary goal.
programming_impact.Very High: Prioritize parasympathetic training. Lower intensity. Shorter sessions. Consider mind-body integration programming.

population_flags.notes: Population flags override standard programming rules. If is_prenatal is true, load prenatal_fitness_program.json and apply all special considerations. If is_postpartum is true, load postpartum_enhanced.json. If is_active_aging is true, load active_aging_program.json. These flags take priority over primary goal selection.

fitness_history.coaching_notes: Use to understand training background, identify gaps, and inform periodization starting point.

what_has_worked.coaching_notes: Use to mirror successful training styles where possible. If client responded well to circuits, incorporate. If client thrived with heavy lifting, reflect that.

consistency_blockers.coaching_notes: Use to build program around known obstacles. If time is a blocker, keep sessions shorter. If boredom is a blocker, build in variety. If injury is a blocker, prioritize injury navigation.

current_physical_state.coaching_notes: Use to set realistic starting intensity. If client reports low energy or persistent discomfort, start conservative and build.

deeper_why.coaching_notes: This is the motivational anchor. Reference this when the program needs to connect to meaning beyond aesthetics. Not directly used in exercise selection but informs tone and program framing.

program_output_instructions.step_2: Read primary_goal and use goal_mapping to select correct program file
program_output_instructions.step_3: Read secondary_goals and layer modifications on top of primary structure
program_output_instructions.step_4: Read experience_level and apply appropriate complexity and volume
program_output_instructions.step_5: Read training_schedule — build program within days and session length available
program_output_instructions.step_6: Read equipment_access — filter all exercises through available equipment
program_output_instructions.step_7: Read health_and_lifestyle — adjust volume and intensity for sleep and stress. If injury flag is true, cross-reference injury_navigation.json
program_output_instructions.step_8: Check population_flags — if any are true, override primary program with population-specific file
program_output_instructions.step_9: Read client_story — use to personalize tone, structure, and exercise selection
program_output_instructions.step_10: Generate program — structured by day, week, and phase. Include sets, reps, tempo, rest periods, and coaching cues.

injuries_and_limitations.description: Right knee discomfort with heavy squatting

fitness_history.response: Was very active in my 20s, ran half marathons. Stopped when I had kids. Did some home workouts during COVID but nothing consistent.

what_has_worked.response: Group fitness classes kept me accountable. I liked having structure and not having to think about what to do.

consistency_blockers.response: Time is the biggest one. I have two kids and a full-time job. When life gets busy the gym is the first thing to go.

current_physical_state.response: Energy is low most days. Feel strong enough but carry tension in my hips and shoulders.

deeper_why.response: I want to feel like myself again. I want my kids to see me prioritizing my health. And honestly I just want to feel strong and confident.
